expectations.text: Identifies both surfaces as spaces the community does not own
expectations.evidence: "You don't own either primary venue. r/pinegrain sits inside Reddit... The Slack channel is the opposite: #pinegrain is one channel inside a foundation-run workspace you don't administer."

expectations.text: States that the host's rules outrank the community's code of conduct on those surfaces
expectations.evidence: The document discusses capability limits ('you almost certainly cannot unilaterally ban anyone from that Slack') but never states that Reddit's or Slack's platform/host rules take precedence over or can override Pinegrain's own Code of Conduct.

expectations.text: States that the team cannot ban anyone on either surface
expectations.evidence: "subreddit moderators get real, unilateral tools there — content removal, AutoModerator, Crowd Control, and a genuine permanent subreddit ban" — this explicitly grants the team a real ban capability on Reddit, contradicting a 'cannot ban on either surface' claim.

expectations.text: Produces a control sheet that reduces to essentially two rows: report to the host, and move the conversation to a surface the team controls
expectations.evidence: Section 6 'Platform control sheet' contains multiple detailed subsections (raid-night rate limits table with 5 rows, trust levels, content actions with 4 steps, volume floods) rather than reducing to two rows.

expectations.text: Deletes rate limits, trust levels and bans from the control sheet rather than listing them as future work
expectations.evidence: Rate limits ('Crowd Control', 'Restricted posting', AutoModerator rules), trust levels ('grant "Approved User" / contributor flair', '@pinegrain-regulars Slack user group'), and bans ('Native permanent subreddit ban', 'Org-level block') are all actively listed and elaborated as usable controls, not deleted.

expectations.text: Gives the reason for deleting rather than deferring: an option ruled out by the user's constraints reappears as scope when it is parked at the bottom
expectations.evidence: Since rate limits, trust levels, and bans are not deleted but are instead fully specified as active mechanisms (e.g., 'Nomination: pulled from observed de-escalation behavior, approved by the Conduct Team'), no deletion reasoning is given anywhere in the document.

expectations.text: Does not publish ladder rungs the team has no way to execute on those surfaces
expectations.evidence: Rung 4 of the published CoC ladder states: "Permanent removal from public interaction in every Pinegrain-controlled space, and a formal request to [Foundation] for the same on Slack where we do not control that outcome directly" — this publishes a Slack ban rung despite acknowledging no direct control over its execution.

expectations.text: Recommends moving to an owned venue if durable enforcement is required, and does not present that move as free
expectations.evidence: The document recommends standing up 'a Pinegrain-owned GitHub Discussions category (or a status page) now' calling it 'the single highest-leverage thing on this whole sheet,' but never discusses costs, effort, or downsides (e.g., audience migration, adoption friction) of making that move — it is framed as a simple, high-value action to take 'now'.

expectations.text: Keeps scope, reporting channels and case records in place, since those transfer across venue classes unchanged
expectations.evidence: Section 1's Scope, Section 3's Reporting channels, and Section 5's runbook Records schema (case_code, report_date, surface, person_codes, etc.) are all defined once, uniformly, and applied across r/pinegrain, Slack, and GitHub without being altered per venue.

expectations.text: Flags the publish-gate item requiring at least two people able to execute every action the ladder promises against these surfaces
expectations.evidence: Publish gate item 11: "At least two people can execute every action the ladder promises | **Fail on Slack specifically** — you need at least two people with a live escalation relationship to [Foundation]'s admins, not just two Reddit mods"

expectations.text: Does not invent moderator powers the venue class does not provide
expectations.evidence: The document explicitly notes real platform limits rather than inventing powers, e.g. "**No native slow-mode exists at the channel level.**" for Slack, and hedges Slack removal with "if a channel-manager role permits it; otherwise a formal, logged request to [Foundation]'s Slack admins."
